_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Afghanistan covering BMAC, Gandhara, Achaemenid satrapies, Alexander the Great, Greco-Bactrian kingdom, Kushan Empire and Gandharan Buddhism, Hephthalites, Ghaznavids, Ghorids, Mongol invasion, Timurid renaissance (Herat), Durrani Empire, Anglo-Afghan Wars, Amanullah reforms, Soviet invasion, mujahideen, Taliban, US intervention 2001, republic era, and Taliban return 2021.

country_profile.government_type: Islamic Emirate (Taliban de facto government since August 2021; internationally unrecognised)

ethnic_groups.name: Pashtun
ethnic_groups.notes: Largest group; south and east; Pashto-speaking; tribal confederations: Durrani (Abdali) and Ghilzai; Pashtunwali code; historically ruling elite; cross-border with Pakistan (FATA/KPK); Taliban predominantly Pashtun

ethnic_groups.name: Tajik
ethnic_groups.notes: Dari-speaking; north and west; Panjshir, Herat, Kabul; Northern Alliance core; Ahmad Shah Massoud's group; urban professionals; Sunni

ethnic_groups.name: Hazara
ethnic_groups.notes: Central highlands (Hazarajat/Bamiyan); Mongol features; Shia Muslim; historically persecuted; Dari-speaking; targeted by Taliban

ethnic_groups.name: Uzbek
ethnic_groups.notes: Northern provinces (Faryab, Jowzjan, Sar-e Pol); Turkic; Abdul Rashid Dostum's group; horse culture; buzkashi

ethnic_groups.name: Aimaq
ethnic_groups.notes: Western/central highlands; semi-nomadic; Dari-speaking; Chahar Aimaq (four tribes): Taimani, Firozkohi, Jamshidi, Hazara-e Aimaq

ethnic_groups.name: Turkmen
ethnic_groups.notes: Northwest (Faryab, Badghis); Turkic; carpet weaving; cross-border with Turkmenistan

ethnic_groups.name: Baloch
ethnic_groups.notes: Southwest (Nimroz, Helmand); cross-border with Pakistan and Iran; Balochi-speaking; pastoral

ethnic_groups.name: Nuristani
ethnic_groups.notes: Nuristan province; last to convert to Islam (1896, formerly 'Kafiristan'); Indo-Aryan languages; mountain people

ethnic_groups.name: Pashai
ethnic_groups.notes: Eastern Afghanistan (Laghman, Nangarhar); Indo-Aryan Pashai language; mountain valleys

ethnic_groups.name: Other (Qizilbash, Brahui, Pamiri, etc.)
ethnic_groups.notes: Qizilbash (Shia, Kabul, historically bureaucratic class); Brahui; Pamiri; Gujars; Jat; Kuchi (nomadic Pashtuns ~2.5M)

independence.from: United Kingdom (Treaty of Rawalpindi; full sovereignty)

current_leader.name: Hibatullah Akhundzada
current_leader.title: Supreme Leader (Amir al-Mu'minin)
current_leader.notes: Taliban; reclusive; rules from Kandahar; women banned from education and work; internationally unrecognised

former_presidents.name: Hamid Karzai
former_presidents.notes: First post-Taliban president; Pashtun (Popalzai); installed after Bonn Conference; corruption issues; eventually anti-US rhetoric

former_presidents.name: Ashraf Ghani
former_presidents.notes: Pashtun (Ahmadzai); World Bank academic; fled as Taliban took Kabul August 15, 2021; exile in UAE

former_presidents.name: Mohammad Najibullah
former_presidents.notes: PDPA/Watan; Soviet-backed; survived 3 years after Soviet withdrawal; killed by Taliban 1996

former_presidents.name: Babrak Karmal
former_presidents.notes: PDPA Parcham; installed by Soviet invasion December 1979

former_presidents.name: Mohammad Daoud Khan
former_presidents.notes: Abolished monarchy (cousin King Zahir Shah); first president; killed in Saur Revolution (communist coup) April 1978

former_presidents.name: Mohammed Zahir Shah
former_presidents.notes: Last king; 40-year reign; constitutional monarchy 1964; 'Golden Age' of Afghanistan; overthrown by Daoud; returned from exile 2002 as 'Father of the Nation'; died 2007

910.name: Ancient Gandhara and Bactria
910.description: The Bronze Age civilizations of the Afghan region including Mundigak and Shortugai outposts of the Indus Valley, the Oxus civilization (BMAC), and the development of early Gandharan and Bactrian cultures.

sub_clusters.name: Bronze Age Settlements and BMAC
sub_clusters.description: The Bactria-Margiana Archaeological Complex (BMAC), Mundigak as a proto-urban center in Kandahar, Shortugai as a Harappan trading outpost on the Oxus, and lapis lazuli trade with Mesopotamia.

sub_clusters.name: Early Gandhara and Vedic Period
sub_clusters.description: The Indo-Aryan migrations through the Hindu Kush passes, the region of Gandhara mentioned in the Rigveda, and the establishment of early kingdoms in the Kabul and Swat valleys.
key_events: Gandhara appears as a Mahajanapada in early Indian texts (c. 600 BC)

910.name: Achaemenid and Hellenistic Afghanistan
910.description: Persian Achaemenid control of the region as satrapies of Gandhara, Arachosia, and Bactria, Alexander the Great's campaigns, and the Greco-Bactrian Kingdom's remarkable Hellenistic civilization.

sub_clusters.name: Achaemenid Satrapies
sub_clusters.description: Darius I's incorporation of Gandhara, Arachosia, Sattagydia, and Bactria as eastern satrapies of the Persian Empire, their tribute and military contributions, and the Royal Road connections.

sub_clusters.name: Alexander and Greco-Bactrian Kingdom
sub_clusters.description: Alexander the Great's fierce campaigns in Afghanistan, the founding of cities like Alexandria-in-Arachosia (Kandahar), and the independent Greco-Bactrian Kingdom as the easternmost outpost of Hellenism.
key_events: Alexander the Great founds Alexandria-in-Arachosia (Kandahar) and crosses the Hindu Kush (329 BC)
Greco-Bactrian king Demetrius I invades India, beginning the Indo-Greek period (c. 185 BC)

910.name: Kushan Empire and Gandharan Buddhism
910.description: The Yuezhi migration, the rise of the Kushan Empire connecting China, India, and Rome via the Silk Road, the flourishing of Gandharan Buddhist art, and the colossal Bamiyan Buddhas.

sub_clusters.name: Indo-Greek and Indo-Scythian Period
sub_clusters.description: The Indo-Greek kings of Gandhara including Menander I (Milinda), the Indo-Scythian (Saka) and Indo-Parthian migrations, and the synthesis of Greek, Indian, and Central Asian cultures.

sub_clusters.name: Kushan Zenith under Kanishka
sub_clusters.description: The Kushan Empire under Kanishka the Great, the flowering of Gandharan Greco-Buddhist art, the Fourth Buddhist Council, Silk Road trade, and Peshawar as a great Buddhist capital.
key_events: Kanishka I convenes the Fourth Buddhist Council and patronizes Mahayana Buddhism (c. 127 AD)
Gandharan sculptors create the first anthropomorphic representations of the Buddha

sub_clusters.name: Late Kushan and Kidarites
sub_clusters.description: The decline of Kushan power, Sassanid Persian encroachments from the west, the Kidarite Huns' emergence, and the continued carving of the great Bamiyan Buddhas.

920.name: Hephthalite and Turk Shahi Period
920.description: The White Hun (Hephthalite) conquest, the destruction of Buddhist monasteries, the Turk Shahi and Hindu Shahi dynasties of Kabul, and the initial Arab raids into the region.

sub_clusters.name: Hephthalite (White Hun) Domination
sub_clusters.description: The Hephthalite invasion from Central Asia, the devastation of Buddhist sites in Gandhara, King Mihirakula's brutal reign, and the eventual defeat by a Sassanid-Turkic alliance.
key_events: Hephthalites under Mihirakula devastate Buddhist monasteries across Gandhara (c. 515 AD)

sub_clusters.name: Turk Shahi and Hindu Shahi Kabul
sub_clusters.description: The Western Turkic and Turk Shahi control of Kabul and Gandhara, the Hindu Shahi dynasty's resistance against Arab expansion, and the survival of Buddhist and Hindu cultures.

920.name: Ghaznavid and Ghurid Empires
920.description: The Turkic Ghaznavid Empire based in Ghazni, Mahmud of Ghazni's raids into India, the Ghurid dynasty's conquest, and Afghanistan as the launchpad for Muslim rule in South Asia.

sub_clusters.name: Mahmud of Ghazni and Ghaznavid Empire
sub_clusters.description: Sultan Mahmud of Ghazni's seventeen raids into India, Ghazni as a magnificent capital rivaling Baghdad, the patronage of Ferdowsi and Al-Biruni, and the Ghaznavid cultural legacy.
key_events: Mahmud of Ghazni raids the Somnath temple, one of seventeen campaigns into India (1025 AD)
Al-Biruni writes Kitab al-Hind, a systematic study of Indian civilization (c. 1030 AD)

sub_clusters.name: Ghurid Dynasty and Delhi Sultanate Origins
sub_clusters.description: The rise of the Ghurid dynasty from the mountains of Ghor, Muhammad of Ghor's conquest of northern India, and the foundation of the Delhi Sultanate by Ghurid generals.
key_events: Muhammad of Ghor defeats Prithviraj III at the Second Battle of Tarain, opening India to Muslim rule (1192 AD)

930.name: Mongol Invasion and Timurid Afghanistan
930.description: Genghis Khan's devastating invasion destroying Balkh and Bamiyan, the Kartid dynasty of Herat, and the Timurid Renaissance centered on Herat as one of the great cultural capitals of the Islamic world.

sub_clusters.name: Mongol Devastation
sub_clusters.description: Genghis Khan's annihilation of Balkh and Bamiyan (where his grandson was killed), centuries of depopulation and destruction, and the Kartid dynasty's survival in Herat.
key_events: Genghis Khan destroys Balkh and Bamiyan, ordering the total massacre of Bamiyan's population (1221)
The Kartid dynasty rules Herat as Mongol vassals, preserving Persian culture (1245–1381)

sub_clusters.name: Timurid Herat Renaissance
sub_clusters.description: Timur's conquest and Herat's emergence under Sultan Husayn Bayqara as the greatest cultural center of the Islamic world, the Herat school of miniature painting under Behzad, and the poetry of Jami.
key_events: Sultan Husayn Bayqara rules Herat, presiding over one of Islam's greatest cultural renaissances (1469–1506)

930.name: Mughal-Safavid Rivalry and Durrani Empire
930.description: Babur's use of Kabul as a springboard to conquer India, the Mughal-Safavid contest over Kandahar, Ahmad Shah Durrani's founding of modern Afghanistan, and the first British encounters.

sub_clusters.name: Babur and Mughal Control
sub_clusters.description: Babur's conquest of Kabul and its use as a base to invade India, the strategic Mughal-Safavid competition over Kandahar, and Afghanistan as a contested frontier between empires.
key_events: Babur captures Kabul and uses it as a base to conquer the Delhi Sultanate at Panipat (1504–1526)

sub_clusters.name: Ahmad Shah Durrani and the Afghan State
sub_clusters.description: Ahmad Shah Durrani's founding of the Durrani Empire — the origin of modern Afghanistan — his defeat of the Marathas at Panipat, and the fragmentation under his successors.
key_events: Ahmad Shah Durrani founds the Durrani Empire, the largest Muslim empire of the 18th century (1747)
Third Battle of Panipat — Durrani forces defeat the Maratha Confederacy (1761)

940.name: Great Game and Anglo-Afghan Wars
940.description: Afghanistan as the central arena of the Great Game between the British and Russian empires, three Anglo-Afghan Wars, and Afghanistan's fierce defense of independence.

sub_clusters.name: First Anglo-Afghan War
sub_clusters.description: Britain's disastrous invasion of Afghanistan to install a puppet ruler, the retreat from Kabul, and the annihilation of the 16,500-strong British-Indian column — one of the greatest military disasters in British history.
key_events: Retreat from Kabul — virtually the entire British-Indian force of 16,500 is annihilated (January 1842)

sub_clusters.name: Second and Third Anglo-Afghan Wars
sub_clusters.description: The Second Anglo-Afghan War establishing British control of Afghan foreign policy, the iron rule of Abdur Rahman Khan, and the Third Anglo-Afghan War securing full independence.
key_events: Treaty of Gandamak — Afghanistan becomes a British protectorate in foreign affairs (1879)
Third Anglo-Afghan War — Afghanistan regains full independence (1919)

940.name: Modernization and Monarchy
940.description: Amanullah Khan's ambitious modernization reforms, the tribal backlash, Zahir Shah's long stable reign, the 1964 constitution, and Daoud Khan's republican coup.

sub_clusters.name: Amanullah Reforms and Tribal Reaction
sub_clusters.description: King Amanullah Khan's sweeping secular modernization inspired by Atatürk, the conservative tribal revolt forcing his abdication, and the bandit king Habibullah Kalakani's brief rule.
key_events: Amanullah attempts radical modernization including unveiling; forced to abdicate by tribal revolt (1929)

sub_clusters.name: Zahir Shah Era
sub_clusters.description: King Zahir Shah's four-decade reign providing unprecedented stability, the 1964 constitution introducing democratic reforms, Cold War aid from both superpowers, and Daoud Khan's coup ending the monarchy.

950.name: Soviet-Afghan War
950.description: The Saur Revolution, the Soviet invasion, the decade-long guerrilla war by the mujahideen, the Soviet withdrawal, and the fall of the Najibullah government.

sub_clusters.name: Saur Revolution and Soviet Invasion
sub_clusters.description: The communist Saur Revolution, the People's Democratic Party's radical reforms provoking rebellion, and the Soviet Union's fateful decision to invade Afghanistan.
key_events: Saur (April) Revolution brings the communist PDPA to power (April 1978)
Soviet Union invades Afghanistan with 100,000 troops (December 1979)

sub_clusters.name: Mujahideen Resistance and Soviet Withdrawal
sub_clusters.description: The CIA-backed mujahideen guerrilla war, the introduction of Stinger missiles, the Geneva Accords, the Soviet withdrawal, and the eventual fall of Kabul to mujahideen factions.
key_events: US supplies Stinger missiles to mujahideen, shifting the air war (1986)
Soviet forces complete withdrawal from Afghanistan (February 1989)

950.name: Taliban Rise and US Intervention
950.description: The devastating civil war between mujahideen factions, the Taliban's emergence and capture of Kabul, the harsh Taliban regime, al-Qaeda's presence, and the US invasion after 9/11.

sub_clusters.name: Civil War and Taliban Takeover
sub_clusters.description: The brutal civil war destroying Kabul, the Taliban's rise from Kandahar madrasas, their capture of Kabul, the destruction of the Bamiyan Buddhas, and the sheltering of Osama bin Laden.
key_events: Taliban capture Kabul and impose strict Islamic rule (September 1996)
Taliban destroy the ancient Bamiyan Buddhas despite international outcry (March 2001)

sub_clusters.name: US Invasion — Operation Enduring Freedom
sub_clusters.description: The September 11 attacks, the US ultimatum to the Taliban, Operation Enduring Freedom, the fall of the Taliban regime, and the Bonn Agreement establishing a new government.
key_events: US launches Operation Enduring Freedom after Taliban refuse to surrender Osama bin Laden (October 2001)

960.name: Islamic Republic and NATO Mission
960.description: The Karzai and Ghani governments, the US and NATO military presence, the Taliban insurgency, nation-building efforts, and the Doha Agreement leading to withdrawal.

sub_clusters.name: Karzai Era and Insurgency
sub_clusters.description: Hamid Karzai's transitional and elected governments, the reconstitution of the Taliban insurgency, the US troop surge, and the killing of Osama bin Laden in Pakistan.
key_events: Hamid Karzai elected president in Afghanistan's first democratic election (2004)
US Navy SEALs kill Osama bin Laden in Abbottabad, Pakistan (May 2011)

sub_clusters.name: Ghani Government and Doha Agreement
sub_clusters.description: President Ashraf Ghani's government, the drawdown of NATO forces, the US-Taliban Doha Agreement excluding the Afghan government, and the stage set for Taliban return.

960.name: Taliban Restoration and Humanitarian Crisis
960.description: The rapid Taliban takeover as US forces withdrew, the chaotic Kabul airport evacuation, the reimposition of Taliban rule, the ban on women's education, and the severe humanitarian crisis.

sub_clusters.name: Fall of Kabul 2021
sub_clusters.description: The lightning Taliban offensive overrunning provincial capitals, President Ghani's flight, the chaotic evacuation at Kabul airport, and the Abbey Gate bombing killing 13 US servicemembers and 170 Afghans.
key_events: Taliban capture Kabul as President Ghani flees; chaotic evacuations at Hamid Karzai Airport (August 2021)
ISIS-K suicide bombing at Abbey Gate kills 13 US troops and approximately 170 Afghans (August 26, 2021)

sub_clusters.name: Second Taliban Emirate
sub_clusters.description: The Taliban's Islamic Emirate government, the progressive ban on women's education and employment, international isolation, economic collapse, and one of the world's worst humanitarian crises.

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
